transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 49m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Tomas Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Sableware ML Lead), Mark Feld (Sableware SRE), Aisha Gomez (Sableware Product)

Auto-summary (brief): We went through the scorecard heatmap and focused on ~120 failing examples; narrowed to top 40. Discussed adjustment to pass/fail thresholds, a small model variant fallback, and guardrail exception handling. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. audio? good?
[00:04] Priya Nair: Yep can hear you, good. Sorry run over from stand-up so a bit late.
[00:08] Maya Chen: No worries. Quick agenda, triage the newest scorecard spikes, propose threshold changes, and decide if we need immediate rollback playbook. Tomas will walk the numbers.
[00:18] Tomas Rivera: Cool, I uploaded the heatmap to the shared pilot dashboard, file name is "sable-pilot-heatmap-v7.csv". Quick note, some of the transcriptions tag Redwood product as "Redwood Dedicate" in the logs, ignore that — it's Redwood Dedicated.
[00:33] Priya Nair: Ha yeah saw that, the ai transcript spelled stuff funny. So main ask: we had a jump in hallucination rate over the last three days after the prompt set expansion. want to understand root cause.
[00:44] Tomas Rivera: Right. We split failures into three buckets: hallucination (45%), truncation/length limit artifacts (30%), and safety false positives (25%). The hallucination cluster seems concentrated on prompts that use multi-turn references with long legal snippets — the KV cache sometimes misses a previous context token in the trimmed window.
[01:05] Mark Feld: Quick question, are you seeing this on Hosted only or on Dedicated routing too? We routed 20% of calls to Dedicated yesterday for the smoke.
[01:12] Tomas Rivera: We replicated the spike on Hosted and on Dedicated variant with the same model family. There's a small discrepancy in average latency but not significant enough to explain hallucinations. likely prompt engineering/score thresholds.
[01:25] Aisha Gomez: For product perspective: the user-facing failure is that the assistant invents citations in the legal summaries which is a showstopper. Need either filter or a fallback to safe stub.
[01:36] Priya Nair: Agreed. We flagged 12 examples where the output contained fabricated statutes. that's our high severity set.
[01:44] Maya Chen: ok let's walk the recalibration options. Tomas?
[01:47] Tomas Rivera: Option A: tighten the hallucination threshold — raise the precision bar on attribution checks and drop recall slightly. Option B: add explicit guardrail step: if the confidence or citation-score below X, respond with a standard "I don't have a verifiable source" template. Option C: model fallback to a smaller, conservative variant for these prompt families.
[02:10] Priya Nair: Option B seems safer for now because we don't want to change latency profile. But will that increase the rate of false negatives where it withholds correct info?
[02:20] Tomas Rivera: There's a tradeoff. In our sample sweep Option B reduced hallucinations by 60% but increased conservative responses by 8%. Option C reduced hallucinations by 80% but added ~40-60ms median latency and higher token cost.
[02:36] Mark Feld: On cost - we need to see delta which is why Maya will share pricing sketch. If QPS is steady, a 50ms median bump might be acceptable for legal flows.
[02:48] Maya Chen: I'll include a line-item for model variant fallback in the pricing note.
[02:52] Priya Nair: Another issue is truncation: some of our legal snippets are 6-8k tokens. the runtime is trimming mid-sentence and the model hallucinates missing clauses. Is the KV cache being used as a prefix in the Dedicated config?
[03:07] Tomas Rivera: Yes, but the cache compaction policy currently trims by recentness not semantic boundaries. We can update the compaction window to preserve sentence boundaries for long docs; that reduces truncation artifacts but increases memory slightly.
[03:20] Priya Nair: What's the memory impact? our dedicated pool has fixed capacity.
[03:24] Tomas Rivera: In our bench it was ~12% higher GPU memory per instance for those prompt families. but we can tune batch sizes. We'll run a targeted bench.
[03:33] Mark Feld: That bench is critical — we need numbers before we commit to compaction changes. Could provision a test node.
[03:38] Tomas Rivera: Great, we'll schedule the latency/memory bench.
[03:41] Maya Chen: On safety false positives — there's a cluster where the guardrail flags benign language because of older regex rules. We should add allowlist for domain-specific phrases.
[03:52] Aisha Gomez: Example?
[03:53] Priya Nair: We saw "safe harbor" flagged in three cases — it's a legitimate term.
[03:57] Tomas Rivera: We'll add a domain allowlist and create an exception path in the guardrail engine to surface instead of block. That will reduce false positives and preserve audit logs.
[04:08] Maya Chen: Ok, let's capture immediate remediations: 1) tighten hallucination threshold + template fallback (fast), 2) allowlist for domain terms (fast), 3) compaction policy tweak and bench (medium), 4) consider model fallback for highest severity flows (decision after bench).
[04:25] Priya Nair: Sounds good. For the sweep Tomas — can you also annotate which failures are "behavioral" vs "infrastructure"? So our PM can prioritize.
[04:34] Tomas Rivera: Yep I'll tag them in the csv. note: transcription sometimes labels the SE as Speaker 2, so the file may show odd headers.
[04:44] Mark Feld: Quick point on security/compliance: we'll need the KMS integration doc and the SOC2 snapshot. Can you send those?
[04:50] Maya Chen: Yes, I will share our SOC2 summary and the KMS/HSM integration checklist. For on-prem, we have an extra checklist that Priya might want.
[04:58] Priya Nair: We will need the on-prem checklist. Also can you confirm retention for logs? legal needs 90 days of redacted transcripts.
[05:06] Maya Chen: Default retention for Hosted pilot is 30 days but we can extend to 90 for pilot under the trial terms, and for Dedicated you can configure longer retention. I'll document that.
[05:15] Tomas Rivera: Two more technical notes: 1) prefix caching sometimes returns stale keys when rapidly alternating contexts — we need to bump cache TTL for legal flow. 2) We saw some tokenization edge-cases with the vendor doc encoding; we'll provide a sanitization snippet.
[05:35] Priya Nair: Good call. The doc encoding issue explains a handful of weird tokens.
[05:40] Aisha Gomez: On rollout cadence — what's realistic for guardrail changes? we'd like an initial fix within a week and a more thorough rollback playbook in two weeks.
[05:48] Maya Chen: Agreed. We'll aim for a small guardrail patch in 5 business days and a formal rollback/canary playbook within 10 business days.
[05:58] Priya Nair: Can you also send the sample canary metrics you'd monitor? latency, hallucination rate, safety flags, cost per 1k tokens?
[06:06] Tomas Rivera: We'll share a monitoring template — it includes hallucination FPR/TPR, median latency, 95th latency, per-route cost, and guardrail exception rates.
[06:15] Maya Chen: Any other blockers from the customer side?
[06:18] Mark Feld: We want the bench to happen earlier if possible. I'll try to prioritize VPC access.
[06:23] Priya Nair: Also want slightly more context in the heatmap lines — a short text snippet so we can triage faster.
[06:29] Tomas Rivera: I'll add a 200-char snippet column and re-upload.
[06:32] Maya Chen: Perfect. Let's recap next steps, owners, and due dates.

Recap / Next steps (spoken):
[06:38] Maya Chen: Tomas runs 3k sweep + tags infra vs behavior (due 12/22).
[06:43] Tomas Rivera: Yep.
[06:44] Maya Chen: Maya sends pricing and SOC2/KMS docs, on-prem checklist, and model fallback cost line (due 12/18).
[06:51] Priya Nair: We'll upload the 40 highest-severity prompts and prioritize them (due 12/21).
[06:56] Mark Feld: I'll provision a test VPC and share creds for the bench (target 12/20).
[07:02] Maya Chen: Schedule a deep-dive next week for caching behavior after bench results.
[07:06] Priya Nair: ok thanks everyone.
[07:08] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow-up in email with links.

End of meeting.
